text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - Bunds and futures ended the week on a softer note unable to escape the U.S. Treasury market's losses. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.44, down 0.13 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts subsided weakly into the weekend having recovered after a robust set of GDP data early on Friday morning. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 108-23/32, down 10/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond and interest rate futures came under pressure as investors became more concerned about the possibility that the ruling centre-right coalition might not win a majority in an upcoming parliamentary election. The June bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.28, down 0.34 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian financial markets were closed for Liberation Day. Yesterday dealers said markets were a little nervous ahead of Italian local elections on Sunday and a weekend G7 meeting in Washington.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries opened mostly unchanged but are expected to remain under pressure as the market continues to be weighed down by supply, fear of strong data next week and concerns of further rate hikes. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 107-06/32, down 04/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.14 percent.

JAPAN - Government bonds and futures plunged as Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co's business suspension, the first such case among insurers in the postwar period, triggered fears of higher interest rates. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 125.60, down 0.83 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Activity in the Eurobond market tailed off, with a quiet week expected next week. Japanese investors will be out of action for the Golden Week holiday, which ends on May 5. The release of U.S. data would keep many investors sidelined. The market did see a rare Polish zloty-linked bond from Metro Finance. Poland's Bank Handlowy was holding presentations in London for a $200 million Eurobond due next week.
